subject: Re: Private offer packaging options + channel margin evidence

Subject: Private offer: packaging approach + reseller margin 

Evelyn / Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached is a starter SKU list (Stratos_PO_SKUs.xlsx) showing our expected committed reserved capacity per region and a couple of metered add-ons (embedding calls, fine-tune credits).

High-level asks from our side:
- We want a single private offer on AWS covering EU regions but need a clear pass-through for our EU distributor (we pay them a portion of the committed value).
- Target discount vs list: ~28% blended across committed vs metered.
- What channel margin can Redwood support on the private offer path (our distributor expects a visible margin on invoices so they can reconcile with resale rules)?
- We also need evidence we can present to procurement that invoices will show the distributor netback and that reseller credits flow in the same billing cadence.

Can you outline two practical packaging approaches and the operational evidence you will provide (invoices, reseller IDs, and the P&L waterfall)?

Michael

Hi Michael —

Appreciate the SKU list — that’s very helpful. Quick reply with two packaging patterns that are commonly used (and the evidence we can supply) so you and procurement have something to review quickly. I’ve attached a short outline (initial-private-offer-outline.pdf).

Option A — Consolidated commit + metered addons (single private offer):
- Single committed SKU (monthly node-hour equivalent) with a blended list price.
- Metered add-ons billed on usage monthly (embeddings, fine-tune).
- Advantages: one offer, simpler billing, fewer SKUs to manage.
- Channel pass-through: invoices will show the committed line and a separate distribution line identifying the distributor/partner ID so your distributor can reconcile margins.
- Typical allowable distributor margin we can surface on the invoice: 8–14% (higher for named strategic partners, needs review).

Option B — Banded commit (tiered buckets) + explicit reseller voucher lines:
- Commit is split into bands (0–250k, 250–1M, >1M token-equivalent).
- Reseller/broker fees can be modeled as a separate credit/voucher line so netback is explicit per month.
- Advantages: clearer accounting for margin waterfalls; easier to implement staged uplift if commit grows.

Evidence & ops we can provide:
- Example monthly invoice with distributor ID and descriptive line items.
- Reseller-evidence checklist (what procurement requires: reseller agreement, tax IDs, VAT routing guidance).
- DocuSign private offer template and HubSpot deal linkage for audit.

Two quick clarifying questions for procurement:
1) Which distributor/legal entity will appear on invoices (name + VAT)?
2) Do you need the margin expressed as a percent visible on the invoice, or is a separate monthly remittance report sufficient?

If you’re ok with either approach we can choose A for speed or B for accounting clarity. Ben — can you loop in Olga from deal ops to confirm the reseller-evidence flow and timing?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Steve <michael.steve@stratos.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer: packaging approach + reseller margin

Michael / team —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick operational notes from deal ops so procurement can see how this will land:
- Invoice path: we can put the distributor as a separate line item and include the distributor VAT and partner ID in the invoice meta so their finance team can reconcile.
- Margin mechanics: industry-standard visible netback we’ve done recently is 10–12% for EU distributors on private offers; 12% is reasonable for a named strategic distributor given the commit you outlined.
- Broker/interop fee: if you intend to have a broker between you and the distributor we recommend a separate broker fee line (we can support up to 5% as an explicit credit line).
- Billing cadence: monthly invoices with a PDF breakdown and a machine-readable CSV export for reconciliation.

What we need from your procurement to proceed:
1) Distributor legal name + VAT and contact email for invoicing.
2) Formal reseller agreement or the reseller master service agreement (if you have one).
3) Expected first-month committed amount (EUR) so we can author the private offer with the right tiers.

I attached the internal reseller-evidence checklist we will use. Olga — can you confirm required lead time for private offer creation and any EU VAT caveats we should flag (reverse charge, local registration)?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: reseller-evidence-checklist.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Evelyn / Ben —

Appreciate the quick turn. We reviewed Option B internally and prefer the banded commit + explicit reseller voucher line for audit reasons. A few confirmations from our side:
- Distributor entity: Nimbus Distribution Ltd (VAT GB99999997) — they will need a visible 12% margin on the committed line.
- Broker fee: none — Nimbus is our primary distributor.
- First month commit target (EUR): 220,000.
- Procurement requires the invoice sample (with distributor line) plus a short note on SLA commitments tied to private offer (latency SLA for reserved nodes and remediation credits).

If you can provision the draft private offer (Option B) with the bands and include a sample invoice by EOB Monday Europe time that would help our procurement queue. I can sign off quickly once we see the invoice flow and the DocuSign PO.

Onward —
Michael
